title: Touring at twelve and playing pig stands
summary: Summer tours with Doc Palmer at twelve, then Sunday pig-stand gigs working for tips that Doc split.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So I had the experience of working with these guys with Doc's band. That's what really got me on the road. We'd go out on tours during the summer, and it was a spectacular feat(?) at 12 years old going out on a tour, you know.
Yeah, my people let me go out on a tour with them, you know.

Yeah, we played dance ballrooms, you know -- mostly. Then sometimes I would work in a small group with Doc, and another friend of mine, a saxophone player named Ricky Roseman(?). Ricky also played with Doc's band at different times. And we worked at what they called then Pig-Stands, which later became drive-ins. You know, they used to sell pig...pork sandwiches on a bun. And we would out in the front of the places...out in front. And no salary. Doc would pass the hat around the crowd, and people

would make requests and tip; tip us for playing the requests. So that's how we made... Because all we'd get was a sandwich. Actually, we'd get a break, and we could get a sandwich. But we made pretty good dough...
Doc would split the tips with us. And it was quite something.

Oh, sometimes we would make... It was on Sundays when we played the pig-stands, sometimes Saturday, but usually on Sundays... On the weekends, in the afternoons, we played the pig-stands. And sometimes you could come out with two or three dollars a piece, which was big money in those days.
